title: Eating Well When You're Pregnant
hook: Most foods are fine in pregnancy — but a short list carries infection or toxin risks worth knowing, alongside a daily folic acid supplement and a varied, balanced diet.
key_points: Build meals around plenty of fruit and veg, starchy carbs, protein, and dairy — there's no need to 'eat for two'.
Avoid high-mercury fish (shark, swordfish, marlin) and limit oily fish and tuna; these carry mercury or pollutants.
Skip unpasteurised and mould-ripened soft cheeses, raw or undercooked meat, liver, and raw/partially cooked eggs (listeria, salmonella, vitamin A).
Avoid alcohol entirely and keep caffeine under about 200mg a day; keep taking a folic acid supplement.
content_html: You don't need to "eat for two" in pregnancy — you need to eat well. A varied, balanced diet built around fruit and vegetables, starchy carbohydrates, protein, and dairy covers most of what you and your baby need, alongside a daily folic acid supplement that the NHS recommends throughout the first trimester.
extra_html: The bigger thing to learn is the short list of foods to be careful with, because pregnancy raises the stakes on certain infections and toxins. The NHS advises avoiding high-mercury fish (shark, swordfish, marlin) and limiting oily fish and tuna; skipping unpasteurised and mould-ripened soft cheeses, raw or undercooked meat, liver, and raw or partially cooked eggs that aren't British Lion stamped; avoiding alcohol entirely; and keeping caffeine under about 200mg a day. These guard against risks like listeria, salmonella, and excess vitamin A. This is general guidance — your own midwife or doctor can tailor it to your situation and any specific concerns.

related.title: Folic Acid Before and During Pregnancy
related.hook: Taking folic acid before conception and in early pregnancy is one of the best-evidenced ways to lower the risk of serious birth defects of the brain and spine.

related.title: Why Prenatal Visits Matter
related.hook: Regular checkups during pregnancy catch problems early — for many a typical schedule is monthly, then every two weeks, then weekly as the due date nears.

related.title: The Common Aches of Pregnancy
related.hook: Nausea, heartburn, fatigue, and a sore back are the everyday companions of pregnancy — usually normal and manageable. The skill is knowing the simple fixes, and which symptoms are not on this list.

flashcards.prompt: Which fish should you avoid completely during pregnancy because of mercury?
flashcards.explanation_html: Shark, swordfish, and marlin carry the most mercury. Oily fish like salmon are healthy but the NHS suggests limiting them to about two portions a week.

flashcards.prompt: What's the daily caffeine guideline in pregnancy, and what about alcohol?
flashcards.back_html: Keep caffeine under about 200mg a day (roughly two mugs of instant coffee), and avoid alcohol entirely — there's no known safe amount.

flashcards.prompt: Why avoid unpasteurised and mould-ripened soft cheeses in pregnancy?
flashcards.explanation_html: Unpasteurised and soft mould-ripened cheeses (like brie) carry a small risk of listeria, which can be dangerous in pregnancy.
